The check-in console solved exactly this problem correctly one screen over with `min(300px,70vw)` + `aspect-ratio:1`; face enrolment just did not adopt it. Two camera rings in one module, two different sizing strategies.

pattern: page gutter hardcoded three times, no gutter token, so cards double-inset on mobile ('box-in-box')

pattern: single spacing scale with no mobile step, and off-scale literals throughout the stylesheet
evidence: --lf-space-1..10 = 4,8,12,16,20,24,32,40. rootCause: No :root override exists inside any media query in either file, so mobile inherits desktop spacing verbatim: 22px section gaps and 20-22px card padding on a 358px canvas is why the pages read as a shrunk desktop. The off-scale 18/22px values also mean a token-level fix would miss them.

pattern: type scale bottoms out at 10px with no mobile step; every heading is a hardcoded px literal

rootCause: Two of ~10 display sizes use clamp; the rest are literals. A 34px serif balance figure in a ~170px card, or a 26px page title beside a wrapped action cluster, is the visible 'squeezed desktop'. Meanwhile 10px and 11px are used for form LABELS (.lf-label, 797) and hints (.lf-hint, 841) — legible on a 27" monitor at arm's length, marginal on a phone.

pattern: 9px type used for meaningful, non-decorative labels
evidence: .lf-nav-label{font-size:9px} (245); .lf-table th{font:650 9px/1 …} (480); .lf-grid td::before mobile card label {font:650 9px/1.5} (1279); .lf-table td::before mobile label {9px} (1341); .lf-sidebar-user-copy span{9px} (338); .lf-leave__unpaid{9px} (1828); .lf-users__count{9px} (1966); .lf-users__consent{9px} (1996); .lf-roles__default{9px} (2066)

pattern: compact density mode drops row height to 32px and body text to 12px, with no coarse-pointer guard
evidence: [data-density='compact'] { --lf-row: var(--lf-row-compact); /* 32px */ --lf-text-sm: 0.75rem; /* 12px */ }  consumed by `.lf-grid tbody td { height: var(--lf-row) }` (globals 1038)

rootCause: If a user sets compact on their desktop and the preference is persisted per-account, their phone gets 32px rows with 12px text. Even comfortable (44px) only just clears the touch minimum, and only in the ≥861px table mode.

pattern: radius scale with no mobile values — 6px controls read squared at phone scale
evidence: --lf-radius-sm:6px; --lf-radius:9px; --lf-radius-lg:13px; --lf-radius-xl:16px. Three separate empty-state implementations with three paddings (40/34/20px) and a fourth that is just a bare

evidence: .lf-table-wrap { border:1px solid var(--lf-line); border-radius:var(--lf-radius-lg); box-shadow:var(--lf-shadow-1); }  and .lf-grid-wrap (1003) repeats it; both then contain rows that draw their own `border-bottom:1px solid var(--lf-line)` (488, 1040), and the mobile card modes add a third `border-bottom` per row (1259, 1322)

pattern: sticky thead inside a non-scrolling wrapper slides under the sticky topbar
evidence: .lf-grid thead th { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:2; } with .lf-grid-wrap { overflow:hidden } (1007), while .lf-shell-topbar { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:30; height:56px } (92)

rootCause: Recorded for completeness: this component escapes mobile only because its container is display:none below 820px. The technique (percentage-negative offsets between flex siblings) breaks the moment items are allowed to wrap, which is what any mobile version would need.

pattern: nowrap text nodes with no min-width:0 in flex rows — the classic horizontal-overflow source
evidence: .lf-shell-crumb { flex:none; white-space:nowrap } (1477-1482); .lf-module-panel__link { white-space:nowrap } (2438); .lf-ledger__time { white-space:nowrap } (2507); .lf-eventlist time { white-space:nowrap } (3790); .lf-channel__mode { white-space:nowrap } (4013); .lf-ai-chips a { white-space:nowrap } (2695); .lf-badge { white-space:nowrap } (860); .lf-table th (483) and .lf-grid thead th (1028)

pattern: ten ad-hoc breakpoints with no token scale — components collapse at unrelated widths
primitiveNeeded: a breakpoint token set (--bp-sm 640 / --bp-md 900 / --bp-lg 1200, or PostCSS custom-media) that every new primitive references, and a one-time reconciliation of the existing 20 blocks onto it

pattern: no mobile type/control scale — tokens.css has zero width media queries, so --lf-text-sm stays 13px and every control height stays desktop-sized on a phone
evidence: --lf-text-2xs: 0.625rem; /* 10px */  --lf-text-xs: 0.6875rem; /* 11px */  --lf-text-sm: 0.8125rem; /* 13px — grid body, the workhorse */   … grep '@media' src/styles/tokens.css → only line 189 (prefers-reduced-motion)
rootCause: The design system was authored at one viewport. Sizes are absolute rem values with no viewport step, so 'mobile' is literally the desktop scale rendered narrower — which is exactly the reported symptom.

pattern: sub-44px touch target + iOS focus-zoom trigger on every form control in the product
